claims.statement: C3-T3 proves the registered weighted-Hall saturation statement for stars in the stated range 2<=p<=m-1 and p>(m-1)/2, for any fixed set of leaf tags, using deletion edges. It supplies no proof or refutation of saturation for general ordinary trees under the fixed favorable selector and lower-region guards.
claims.scope: Star trees in the route's displayed rank range are supported; the universal ordinary-tree mechanism at the registered fixed-selector lower-region scope remains open.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the tag-preserving symmetric-chain injection proves the star restriction. The T67 scalar aggregate supplies no set-level flow, matching, or Hall certificate, so the general statement remains unresolved.

claims.statement: For a star K_{1,m}, any fixed subset F of original leaf tags, and 2<=p<=m-1 with p>(m-1)/2, each weighted upper tagged object injects into a weighted lower tagged object by a tag-preserving deletion; consequently the corresponding weighted clone graph saturates its upper supply.
claims.scope: Stars only, arbitrary fixed leaf-tag subset, and the route's displayed Boolean-layer ranks; no favorable-selector or general-tree conclusion.
claims.reason: retained: in the Boolean lattice on m-1 untagged leaves, the symmetric chain through rank p also contains rank p-1 because p>(m-1)/2. Consecutive members differ by one leaf, witness membership holds at both ranks, and retaining the tag preserves injectivity across tags.

claims.statement: The specified T_67 ordinary tree at p=99 is eligible with all 202 original leaves favorable and has the exact complete selected sum recorded in the source evidence.
claims.scope: One tree, recipe, and rank only; bounded exact computation with replay through a scratch copy of the hash-pinned common evaluator.
claims.reason: retained: scratch-copy replay agrees with the complete independence and delta vectors, alpha=203, x=97, both selector-orbit deltas, all 202 favorable leaves, the strict guard 297<407, the two summand classes, and the exact full sum. This verifies one bounded row and gives no flow certificate.

limitations: The T67 replay uses the same listed evaluator implementation as the route and is not an independent dynamic-program implementation.
No set-level T67 flow, matching, or Hall cut was computed; the scalar sum does not certify weighted-Hall saturation.
The symmetric-chain argument proves only the star subcase; the general ordinary-tree mechanism and the full lower-region aggregate remain unresolved by this route.
The T67 computation is one bounded instance, not a census or universal result.
